subject: biology-hl
author: original (NevaIB)
title: Integration of body systems
bigPicture: A body works as one because its parts are coordinated. In animals, nerves give fast, targeted signals, hormones give slower, widespread ones, and the blood carries materials between organs. HL adds how plants coordinate growth with hormones such as auxin, cytokinin and ethylene.

keyIdeas.answer: For the parts of a system to work together to perform an overall function, they must be coordinated.

keyIdeas.cue: How does the hierarchy of subsystems produce emergent properties?
keyIdeas.answer: Cells form tissues, tissues form organs, and organs form systems. Integrating them gives properties no part has alone, e.g. a cheetah's hunting ability comes from integrated muscles, nerves, heart, lungs and eyes.

keyIdeas.cue: Nervous vs endocrine signalling, and the role of blood?
keyIdeas.answer: Nervous: electrical impulses along neurons, very fast, short-lived, targeted. Endocrine: hormones in the blood, slower, longer-lasting, widespread. The blood also transports materials and heat between organs (e.g. glucose from the gut to muscles, urea from liver to kidneys).

keyIdeas.cue: What does the brain do as an integration centre?
keyIdeas.answer: It combines information from many inputs to decide on responses, and it stores information through learning and memory.

keyIdeas.cue: What does the spinal cord integrate?
keyIdeas.answer: Unconscious processes, such as reflexes, without involving the brain. Conscious processes involve awareness and are controlled by the cerebral hemispheres.
Carry impulses from receptors to the central nervous system (spinal cord and brain).
Carry impulses from the CNS (e.g. cerebral hemispheres) to muscles, stimulating them to contract.
A bundle of sensory and motor nerve fibres, some myelinated and some not, surrounded by a protective sheath.

Free nerve ending (pain receptor) in the hand → sensory neuron → one interneuron in the grey matter of the spinal cord → motor neuron → skeletal muscle (effector) contracts to pull the hand away. It is involuntary and fast.
It coordinates skeletal muscle contractions to give smooth, accurate movement and balance.

The pineal gland secretes melatonin when it is dark, so levels rise in the evening and stay high at night, promoting sleep; light suppresses it in the morning. This sets a roughly 24-hour (circadian) sleep–wake cycle.

Secreted by the adrenal glands under stress, it prepares the body for vigorous activity: faster, stronger heartbeat, dilated airways, glycogen broken down to glucose, blood diverted to muscles from the gut, dilated pupils.

keyIdeas.cue: How do the hypothalamus and pituitary control the endocrine system?
keyIdeas.answer: The hypothalamus monitors the body and links the nervous and endocrine systems. It controls the pituitary gland, which secretes hormones that regulate other endocrine glands (e.g. TSH to the thyroid, FSH/LH to the gonads) and some body functions.

Baroreceptors (in the aorta and carotid arteries) sense blood pressure; chemoreceptors (aorta, carotid arteries, brainstem) sense blood pH, O₂ and CO₂. The brainstem (medulla) sends nerve impulses to the SA node to change heart rate and stroke volume.

CO₂ from respiration forms carbonic acid, lowering blood pH. Chemoreceptors in the brainstem detect this, and the brainstem sends impulses to the diaphragm and intercostal muscles to breathe faster and deeper, removing CO₂.

Swallowing and egestion are voluntary (controlled by the CNS). Peristalsis in between, waves of muscle contraction pushing food along, is involuntary and coordinated by the enteric nervous system in the gut wall.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you record tropisms in seedlings?
keyIdeas.answer: Qualitative: labelled drawings of seedling shapes under one-sided light. Quantitative: measure the angle of curvature with a protractor. Precision depends on the measuring tool; accuracy on method.
Directional growth of a shoot towards light coming from one side.
Signalling chemicals that control plant growth, development and responses to stimuli, e.g. auxin, cytokinin, gibberellin, ethylene, abscisic acid.

keyIdeas.cue: How do auxin efflux carriers make a gradient?
keyIdeas.answer: Auxin diffuses into cells but can't diffuse out. Efflux carriers pump it out of one side of each cell; if all cells put their carriers on the same side, auxin is moved from cell to cell and concentrated in one part of the plant (e.g. the shaded side of a shoot).

Auxin makes cells secrete H⁺ into the cell wall (apoplast). The acid loosens cross-links between cellulose fibres so the cell can elongate. With more auxin on the shaded side, those cells grow faster and the shoot bends towards the light.

keyIdeas.cue: How do auxin and cytokinin coordinate roots and shoots?
keyIdeas.answer: Root tips make cytokinin, which travels to the shoots; shoot tips make auxin, which travels to the roots. Their balance integrates root and shoot growth.

keyIdeas.cue: How does positive feedback control fruit ripening?
keyIdeas.answer: Ethylene triggers ripening changes, and ripening fruit makes more ethylene, which spreads to neighbouring fruit. Ripening is therefore rapid and synchronised, which attracts seed-dispersing animals.

keyTerms.def: Property of a whole system not found in its parts.
Neural pathway for a rapid involuntary response.
Nerve network in the gut wall controlling peristalsis.
Growth response towards or away from directional light.

workedExamples.title: Read a melatonin graph
workedExamples.prompt: Melatonin is low from 08:00 to 20:00, rises after 21:00 and peaks around 03:00. Explain the pattern and predict the effect of jet lag.
steps: Darkness stimulates the pineal gland to secrete melatonin.
High melatonin promotes sleep; light in the morning suppresses it.
After flying east the light–dark cycle is shifted, so melatonin peaks at the wrong local time.
workedExamples.answer: Melatonin tracks darkness; jet lag is a mismatch until the rhythm resets.

misconceptions.right: Nerve impulses are much faster; hormone effects last longer.

misconceptions.wrong: Reflexes are controlled by the brain.
misconceptions.right: Simple reflexes are integrated in the spinal cord.

misconceptions.wrong: Auxin makes cells divide on the shaded side.
Plants grow towards light because light pulls them.
